item.title: United Breweries Q2 profit jumps nearly 3x to ₹134.81 cr on volume growth
item.description: Beer maker United Breweries Ltd on Tuesday reported a nearly three-fold jump in consolidated net profit to Rs 134.81 crore in the September quarter, primarily driven by premiumisation, cost efficiency and volume growth. The Dutch multinational brewing company Heineken NV-controlled firm had posted a net profit of Rs 46.34 crore in the July-September period a year ago, according to a regulatory filing. UBL's revenue from operations increased 23.7 per cent year-on-year to Rs 4,623 crore in the September quarter of FY27, compared to Rs 3,737.31 crore in the corresponding period a year ago. "Net Sales grew 24 per cent, driven by strong volume growth, structural price increases, premiumisation, favourable geographic mix and improvement in the company's operating mix," said UBL in its earnings statement. item.description: LT Foods, the maker of Daawat basmati rice, on Tuesday reported a 10 per cent year-on-year rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 180 crore for the September quarter, while revenue grew 17 per cent to Rs 3,253 crore. The company's revenue from operations stood at Rs 2,772 crore in the year-ago period. Net profit was Rs 164 crore in the July-September quarter of the previous fiscal. EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation) rose 13 per cent to Rs 358 crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 316 crore a year earlier. However, profitability margins contracted during the quarter. EBITDA margin declined to 11 per cent from 11.4 per cent a year ago, while net profit margin fell to 5.5 per cent from 5.9 per cent. Gross profit increased 12 per cent to Rs 1,058 crore during the quarter, compared with Rs 948 crore in the corresponding period last fiscal. item.description: Tata Capital on Tuesday reported a 51 per cent growth in consolidated net profit to Rs 1,660 crore for the September quarter of FY27. The company had posted a net profit of Rs 1,097 crore in the July-September period of FY26. Net total income rose 24 per cent to Rs 4,676 crore during the September quarter of FY27, from Rs 3,774 crore in the corresponding period a year ago, the company said in a regulatory filing. Tata Capital Managing Director and CEO, Rajiv Sabharwal, said the company's loan book crossed Rs 3 trillion, "underscoring the scale, diversification and resilience of our franchise". The non-bank lender's Assets Under Management (AUM) stood at Rs 3,08,030 crore, up 26 per cent year-on-year. "Asset quality remained stable, reflecting our continued focus on portfolio quality, prudent underwriting and effective collections," Sabharwal said. item.description: ACC Ltd, an Adani Group cement firm, on Tuesday reported 91.7 per cent fall in consolidated net profit to Rs 93 crore for September quarter FY27, on account of decline in sales volume due to a Master Supply Agreement with the parent entity. The company had posted a profit of Rs 1,119 crore in the July-September period, according to a regulatory filing from ACC, a subsidiary of Ambuja Cements. The year-ago profit "includes income tax provision reversal of Rs 659 crore relating to earlier period and interest on income tax refund of Rs 205 crore." Revenue from operations was down 5.24 per cent year-on-year to Rs 5,656 crore in September quarter FY27. Total expenses were up 2.46 per cent at Rs 5,602 crore. In the quarter, revenue from the cement business was down 6.9 per cent at Rs 5,206 crore. item.title: Anup Bagchi takes charge as HDFC Bank CEO and MD, succeeds Jagdishan
item.description: Country's largest private sector lender HDFC Bank on Tuesday said that Anup Bagchi has taken charge as its managing director and chief executive. His predecessor, Sashidhar Jagdishan, vacated office on Monday after the completion of his term, the bank informed exchanges. Bagchi, an ICICI Group veteran, is the first outsider to head HDFC Bank in its over-three-decade history. His previous assignment was as the MD and CEO of ICICI Prudential Life Insurance. He joins HDFC Bank at a time when the lender is battling a slew of challenges, including ones on core income growth and margins, which have made investors wary. In brief comments on an earnings call which he attended, Bagchi said a part of the work on the bank's 2023 merger with housing finance major parent HDFC is yet to be executed and also announced that he will be meeting all the stakeholders to better understand the bank.
